forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Tamworth took out no new loans in 2025/26 despite £17.2m of capital spending
news_drafts.lead:
Tamworth Borough Council took out no new loans in 2025/26, even though it spent £17.2m on capital spending (money spent on things that last, such as buildings and equipment). The figure is in the annual treasury management report (how the council borrows and invests its cash) that went to its Audit and Governance Committee on 24 September 2026.

The council's total borrowing stayed at £63.060m, unchanged from the year before. The report says the spending was paid for from the council's own cash and from capital receipts (money from asset sales), a practice known as internal borrowing. This saves interest but uses up the council's cash cushion. The report puts the gap between what the council has borrowed and what its capital spending would otherwise require at £7.158m, which it describes as an under-borrowed position.

The council says the reason was cost. In the report's words: "Due to the elevated cost of borrowing long-term, no borrowing was undertaken during the year." The papers describe the approach as a continuing strategy, not a one-year decision.
news_drafts.paper_title: Annual Report on the Treasury Management Service and Actual Prudential Indicators 2025/26 enc. 1

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1a Corporate Risk Register excluding risk 92026
findings.headline: The Local Plan has completed Regulation 19 consultation, with submission preparation for December 2026
findings.detail: The paper says the Local Plan has successfully completed Reg.19 consultation, with climate change embedded. Preparation for submission, including Full Council approval, is due in December 2026.
findings.matters: Completion of a statutory consultation stage is a milestone in the council's planning and housing delivery timetable, and the paper shows the next deadline.
findings.quote: The Local Plan has successfully completed Reg.19 consultation.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1a Corporate Risk Register excluding risk 92026
findings.headline: The environment risk remains at its current score because the service still has no budget allocated
findings.detail: The risk note says the risk remains high because no budget has been allocated to the environmental service. The current score is 12, with a target of 6.
findings.matters: A service with no budget allocation against a net zero commitment is an unfunded obligation that a finance director would want to see stated in a council's own risk paper.
findings.quote: there is still no budget allocated to this service

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1a Corporate Risk Register excluding risk 92026
findings.headline: Market Street refurbishment has a high likelihood of delay to completion due to the condition of the building being "poorer than thought
findings.detail: The Future High Streets Fund project on Market Street is ongoing. The paper says the likelihood of delay to completion is high, and marketing and internal layout work is under way to maximise occupation.
findings.matters: A capital scheme delayed by building condition is a common cost and timing risk for regeneration projects, and other councils would want to compare how it is handled.
findings.quote: Likelihood of delay to completion high due to the condition of the building being poorer than thought.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1a Corporate Risk Register excluding risk 92026
findings.headline: The council states it is highly likely not to be compliant in all areas of the forthcoming housing inspection
findings.detail: The risk note says an improvement plan is underway and that additional resources are being identified. The risk score for legislative compliance is unchanged at 12, with a target of 2.
findings.matters: A stated expectation of non-compliance ahead of an inspection is a compliance signal that a finance director or lender would want to track.
findings.quote: it is highly likely that the council will not be compliant in all areas

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1a Corporate Risk Register excluding risk 92026
findings.headline: The Regulator of Social Housing completed its inspection in July 2026, with the outcome still awaited
findings.detail: The paper says the outcome and the subsequent improvement plan are awaited. It says the improvement plan will replace the Social Housing Regulatory Programme and that this risk will then close. The risk note expects the regulatory inspection outcome at the end of October.
findings.matters: A regulatory intervention on housing would be a material governance event for a council and its lenders, and the paper shows its timing and the process that follows.
findings.quote: Regulator of Social Housing completed inspection in July 2026.

daily_post.headline: The paper states that Tamworth was to become part of the Southern and Mid Staffordshire unitary council on 1st April 2028, and that the timetable is now paused.
daily_post.lead: A council whose future as a standalone authority is uncertain has to plan five years of budgets while the reorganisation timetable is unsettled, which affects lenders and peers alike.
